iron-steel.name: Iron & Steel
iron-steel.seoTitle: CBAM Consulting for Iron & Steel Exporters
iron-steel.seoDescription: CBAM scope, emissions calculation, and reporting obligations for iron and steel products. Expert consulting for manufacturers exporting steel to the EU.
iron-steel.title: CBAM Compliance in the Iron & Steel Sector
iron-steel.intro: Manufacturers exporting crude steel, semi-finished steel products, and various iron and steel goods to the EU face CBAM reporting obligations and, over time, a requirement to purchase certificates. The sector's energy-intensive production routes (blast furnace, electric arc furnace) can make emissions calculation complex.
products: Rolled steel products such as sheet, profile, and pipe
challenges: Accurately reflecting emissions differences between production routes such as blast furnace and electric arc furnace
Managing data collection complexity across a multi-stage production chain (raw material, intermediate, finished product)
Correctly including indirect (electricity-related) emissions in energy-intensive processes

cement.name: Cement
cement.seoDescription: CBAM emissions calculation, reporting, and verification for cement and clinker exports. Consulting for manufacturers exporting cement to the EU.
cement.title: CBAM Compliance in the Cement Sector
cement.intro: Cement production has a high direct emissions intensity due to the calcination reaction in clinker production, making it one of the first sectors covered by CBAM. Manufacturers exporting cement and clinker to the EU must calculate and report their direct emissions per product in line with the EU methodology.
products: Portland cement and various cement types
challenges: Accurately measuring the high direct emissions from calcination in clinker production
Documenting the impact of kiln fuel mix (fossil vs. alternative fuel) on emissions calculation
Building facility-level continuous emissions monitoring infrastructure

aluminium.name: Aluminium
aluminium.seoDescription: CBAM embedded emissions calculation and verification readiness for aluminium products. End-to-end consulting for manufacturers exporting aluminium to the EU.
aluminium.title: CBAM Compliance in the Aluminium Sector
aluminium.intro: Because aluminium production is electricity-intensive, accurately calculating indirect emissions — which depend on the source of the electricity used — is especially critical under CBAM. Manufacturers exporting unwrought aluminium, profiles, sheet, foil, and wire to the EU must report these emissions per product.
challenges: Accurately calculating indirect emissions from the high electricity consumption of the electrolysis process
Documenting the emission factor based on the source of electricity used (grid vs. renewable)
Separating the emissions difference between secondary (recycled) and primary aluminium production

fertilizers.name: Fertilizers
fertilizers.seoDescription: CBAM emissions calculation and reporting obligations for nitrogen-based fertilizer production. Expert consulting for manufacturers exporting fertilizers to the EU.
fertilizers.title: CBAM Compliance in the Fertilizer Sector
fertilizers.intro: The production of nitrogen-based fertilizers and their precursors (such as ammonia and nitric acid) is covered by CBAM due to both energy consumption and process-related greenhouse gas emissions, particularly N2O. Manufacturers exporting fertilizers to the EU must calculate and report these emissions per product.
products: Mixed fertilizers containing nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium
challenges: Accurately measuring and reporting N2O emissions from nitric acid production
Including natural-gas-related emissions from ammonia production in the calculation
Disaggregating product-level emissions for multi-component mixed fertilizers

electricity.name: Electricity
electricity.seoDescription: Consulting on CBAM reporting obligations and direct emissions calculation for electricity exports to the EU.
electricity.title: CBAM Compliance in the Electricity Sector
electricity.intro: Manufacturers exporting electricity to the EU are required under CBAM to report the direct emissions generated from electricity production. Calculation in the electricity sector varies by generation source (thermal, natural gas, renewable, etc.) and requires a transparent, verifiable data infrastructure.
challenges: Accurately documenting emission factors that vary by generation source
Building measurement and verification infrastructure for cross-border electricity trade
Managing the gap between calculations based on actual data and default values

hydrogen.name: Hydrogen
hydrogen.seoDescription: Consulting on CBAM emissions calculation, production-route-based reporting, and verification for hydrogen production and exports.
hydrogen.title: CBAM Compliance in the Hydrogen Sector
hydrogen.intro: Hydrogen can have very different emissions profiles depending on the production method — such as grey, blue, or green hydrogen. Manufacturers exporting hydrogen to the EU must calculate and report emissions specific to their production route under CBAM.
challenges: Correctly classifying the emissions profile based on production route (fossil-based, with carbon capture, renewable)
Documenting the impact of the energy source used in production on emissions calculation
Building verification and reporting infrastructure early in a still-developing market

cbamPage.title: What Is CBAM? Everything You Need to Know
cbamPage.intro: The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) is a European Union regulation designed to prevent carbon leakage and bring non-EU producers into the scope of carbon costs. Companies exporting certain product groups to the EU must report the greenhouse gas emissions generated during production, and over time, pay for those emissions.
cbamPage.whyDescription: CBAM creates both operational and financial obligations for companies exporting to the EU. Businesses caught unprepared risk losing competitiveness through delayed reporting, incomplete data, and unpredictable carbon costs.

timeline.title: Reporting Obligation
timeline.description: Annual emissions reporting becomes mandatory for covered products; there is not yet a financial payment obligation.

timeline.title: Certificate Obligation Begins
timeline.description: Importers become obligated to purchase CBAM certificates corresponding to the embedded emissions of their products.

timeline.title: Scope Expansion
timeline.description: The regulation is expected to expand to additional sectors and to indirect emissions.
